references.text: Aaron and his sons were consecrated to the priestly service, which is confirmed here in Numbers 4 as their responsibility.
The service at the altar, including the incense offering, was reserved for Aaron and his descendants.
The veil (parokhet) is mentioned here as the division between the holy place and the Most Holy Place, where only priests could serve.
Service within the veil was limited to the high priest, and only on the Day of Atonement.
The warning that foreigners who approach shall die is repeated here and emphasizes the exclusive role of the priests.
The foreigner who approaches the tabernacle shall die—the same warning as in Num 18:7.
Korah's rebellion demonstrated the consequences when non-Aaronites attempted to perform priestly service.
Hebrews confirms that no one takes honor for himself as a priest, but must be called by God, just as Aaron was.
Service in the Most Holy Place behind the veil was reserved for the high priest, pointing forward to Christ's perfect priesthood.
